title: I built an inventory auto-battler demo mostly by vibecoding, plus I fine-tuned a diffusion model for the assets
author: rvitor
selftext:
I finally have a playable demo to share.

Stonewake is a run-based inventory auto-battler. The fight is automatic. The real game is the shop and how you place items in a grid. I’m aiming for that feeling where your backpack becomes a little machine: layout, adjacency, and timing create builds that snowball.

Playable demo (itch):

[https://stonewake.itch.io/stonewake](https://stonewake.itch.io/stonewake)

AI angle :

I’ve been programming for 15+ years, but I built most of Stonewake by vibecoding. I still step in for the parts that can ruin a project (architecture, edge cases, balancing), but AI handled a lot of the grind and iteration. I think the hardest problems that AI can face is balancing the game itself.

For visuals, I generated the assets with a diffusion model that I fine-tuned for the project. Then I curated and iterated a lot to keep things consistent.

What I’d love feedback on:

1) After 1–2 rounds, did you understand what your build was trying to do?

2) Did the layout/synergy idea click naturally, or did it feel unclear?

3) Did the shop pacing feel fair, or did you feel forced into bad buys?  


If you try it, tell me what build you went for (even if it failed). The “I thought this would work because…” comments help me tune clarity and progression. 

Hope you play and enjoy it :)

Happy to answer any question you may have.

comments.author: sharkymcstevenson2
comments.body: Looks sick dude, nice work. Could you elaborate more on the workflow to get the visuals and animations etc so tight? I want to get to this level of polish

replies.author: rvitor
replies.body:
Thank you very much. So, I already had some images in an art style I really like very concept-art-like. So I trained a LoRA. I even have a public version of it here:  
[https://civitai.com/models/2376102/fantasy-game-assets-for-z-image-turbo?modelVersionId=2672128](https://civitai.com/models/2376102/fantasy-game-assets-for-z-image-turbo?modelVersionId=2672128)

As for the animations, some, like the home screen, are basically videos made in Gemini on top of an image I generated together with ChatGPT. Some of the UI elements are code. After a lot of attempts and a few manual tweaks, there isn’t really much of a secret, to be honest! When I need to code a visual I normally try to show the model an image, it helps alot.

I hope that was clear and that it helps!

replies.author: rvitor
replies.body: Thank you, hope you can play / did enjoy :)

comments.author: MrFoxChile
comments.body: ¿Algún consejo para un novato que no tiene idea de programación pero si de diseño y una idea de juego? xd

replies.author: rvitor
replies.body:
Creo que deberías probar el *vibecoding*, con herramientas como **Antigravity**, o aprovechar un período gratis en **Codex**. Yo empezaría dibujando las pantallas del juego y descargando algunos *assets* (imágenes) que necesitas para tu juego, o crearlos tú mismo. Luego dile a la IA algo como: “usa los assets que están en la carpeta X” y experimenta con el *vibecoding*; básicamente, está muy bueno y creo que es el futuro de la programación.

Yo sé programar bien, pero siempre vi el código como un medio para lograr algo, no como un fin. Y si quieres aprender a programar, la IA también es una excelente profesora.

AI Translated, hope you can understand!
